summary.tldr: Updates many federal rules to modernize how several regulators, departments and agencies work.
what_it_does: Changes agricultural marketing rules so boards named in the law, not orders, receive delegated powers. It also lets the agriculture minister handle those delegations, requires boards to publish their rules, and repeals some related orders and regulations.
Removes age limits for members of the Canadian Dairy Commission, the National Farm Products Council, and farm product agencies.

Lets the Governor in Council make rules to recognise foreign systems for feeds, fertilisers, seeds, supplements and veterinary biologics. It also changes weed seed rules and lets the agriculture minister approve some outside animal health programs.
Lets the Canadian Food Inspection Agency, the Environment Department and the Fisheries Act use electronic tools for administration and enforcement, and simplifies CFIA reporting.

Changes transport and safety rules, including marine transportation security, railway exemptions, airport land use controls, confidential transport information, and the exclusion of closed loop pumped artificial storage reservoirs from navigable waters.

Creates administrative monetary penalties for some explosives and fisheries violations, updates bankruptcy procedures for small businesses, modernises boards of trade and Canada Lands Surveyors rules, and changes agricultural loan powers.
summary.background: The bill amends many federal laws and regulations to modernize regulatory and administrative processes.
